claims.text: Temperature-dependent magnetometry using VSM or SQUID can test for a ferromagnetic ground state in an AlCoFeNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Nonzero saturation magnetization together with finite coercivity at low temperature confirms a ferromagnetic ground state.
The proposed sample is an as-cast or homogenized AlCoFeNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Co is present in equiatomic or near-equiatomic proportion in the proposed alloy.
Magnetic hysteresis loops should be measured over a range of temperatures using VSM or SQUID.
The characterization should use fields up to several tesla and temperatures from room temperature to approximately 50 K.
The alloy contains stable ferromagnetic domains associated with aligned spins in Co-rich regions.
Exchange interactions among Co and other magnetically active sites produce spontaneous spin alignment.
Spontaneous spin alignment yields measurable remanent magnetization and coercivity.
Below the Curie temperature, the alloy will exhibit a robust hysteresis loop with magnetic saturation and nonzero coercivity.
Paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic states should show weak or no hysteresis under identical measurement conditions.
Paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic states have no spontaneous net magnetization at zero field.
Replacing ferromagnetic species with nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic elements can suppress the net magnetization.
Suppressed net magnetization can mask ferromagnetic ordering in a bulk magnetic measurement.
High-entropy alloys can develop multiphase or heterogeneous microstructures as composition and heat treatment change.
Heterogeneous phases and local compositional variations can complicate magnetic signals and introduce measurement ambiguity.
Magnetic force microscopy or polarized neutron scattering can verify ferromagnetic domain structures.
Failure to measure significant nonzero saturation magnetization or coercivity, or failure to observe stable ferromagnetic domains, would falsify the hypothesis.
